title: Recio Cuatario Review 2026: Legit or Scam?
description: Recio Cuatario review: what its $250 minimum, no-fee claims and 4.6/5 rating say, and where its asset list and broker claims do not match.
author: Sophia Reynolds
excerpt: Recio Cuatario promises AI trading with no fees and a $250 minimum, but its asset list and broker claims do not line up.
content:
Recio Cuatario describes itself as a newly introduced digital asset trading platform. Its page says it combines AI with rule-based models and runs trading automatically, with no human intervention.

This review sets out the terms the page gives, the checks it asks you to make and the points that could not be confirmed from the text alone.

Recio Cuatario at a Glance

The table shows the platform's stated terms. Where the body of the page says something different, the table notes it.

CategoryWhat the page says
Platform typeBrowser-based automated trading, with a user-driven option
Minimum deposit$250
FeesNo sign-up fees and no trading fees
Payment methodsPayPal, Skrill, debit and credit cards, direct bank transfers, or other accepted methods
WithdrawalsGenerally within 24 hours
Asset optionsCryptocurrencies in the table; equities, futures, bonds and derivatives in the text
Regulator or licenceNot stated; the page cites licensed brokers it does not name
OperatorNot named

Items come from the platform's own page. We have not tested the platform or opened an account.

Is Recio Cuatario Legit? What the Claims Show

Recio Cuatario makes claims about its technology, its user ratings and its success rate. Most of them come without figures or sources.

Automation and signals

The page says the system scans the market for trades that match user settings, and it offers a trial mode. Users can choose automatic trading or a user-driven mode. It does not describe the rule-based models, the data they use or how a trade is closed.

Performance and ratings

The page cites a user rating of 4.6/5 without naming a source, and it lists a high success rate among its pros with no numbers. It also says the founders expect users to generate high gains from the initial funding alone. None of this is backed by data in the text.

Asset coverage

The table describes the platform as offering cryptocurrencies, while the body says it supports all major digital currencies and also lists currency pairs, equities, futures, commodities, bonds and derivatives. Before you register, confirm which of these your account can trade.

Costs Worth Knowing

The page says there are no sign-up fees and no trading fees, and that withdrawals are generally processed within 24 hours. It lists no spreads, currency conversion charges or withdrawal limits, so those terms need to come from the operator in writing.

Who Is Behind the Brand

The page calls the platform a browser-based system designed by a group of blockchain followers. No company name, jurisdiction or registration number is given. The sign-up and trading links point to coinpulse.cc, and the page does not say whether that domain belongs to the operator.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Identify the company behind the platform and confirm its registration with a financial regulator.
  • Ask which named brokers hold client funds, then check each licence yourself.
  • Check the asset list inside your account before you deposit, because the table and the text disagree.
  • Keep the first deposit small and note how long withdrawals actually take.

Risks to Keep in Mind

The page says trusting its basic information is not recommended, then concludes that the platform appears to be secure and reliable. It never describes loss of capital as a possibility. The language about substantial growth and large profits is the kind that should be checked independently before any money moves.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the minimum deposit for Recio Cuatario?

The page sets $250. Check the account terms to confirm whether that figure applies to every account type.

Are there any fees?

The page says there are no sign-up or trading fees. It does not list currency conversion costs or the terms that apply after a withdrawal.

Which brokers does Recio Cuatario use?

The page refers to licensed and regulated brokers, but it does not name any of them.

Is the platform available everywhere?

The page says it is not available in Cyprus, Israel or Iran. Check the terms for any other restricted countries before you sign up.

Our Verdict on Recio Cuatario

Recio Cuatario offers a clear entry amount and a trial mode, but its page gives no operator, regulator or evidence for its claims. Our rating reflects those gaps. Confirm the claims through sources outside the platform before anyone deposits funds.
